target: Akita AI Data Center (Bitgrit / S2 Group, Japan)
description: Planned 500MW AI data center in Akita Prefecture, Japan, developed by US startup Bitgrit and local firm S2, targeting operation in the early 2030s at a total build cost near ¥2 trillion (~$12.6B). Abu Dhabi's Mubadala (via its MGX vehicle) is weighing leading up to $6.3B of the financing.

NYSE-listed digital infrastructure investment manager and operator spanning data centers, cell towers, fiber and edge assets. SoftBank Group agreed to acquire it for ~$4.0B ($16.00/share cash) to scale its AI infrastructure push; the deal cleared all regulatory approvals (FERC, CFIUS, antitrust) in September 2026 ahead of closing.

Brookfield Asset Management's dedicated fund for AI-era infrastructure (compute, behind-the-meter power, factories), part of a broader ~$100B AI investment program targeting a $10B first close. NVIDIA and the Kuwait Investment Authority are anchor investors; NVIDIA's commitment was disclosed at $2B.

target: DOE SPARK grid transmission initiative (31 projects, 26 states)
description: US Department of Energy program ("Speed to Power through Accelerated Reconductoring and other Key Advanced Transmission Technology Upgrades") selecting 31 grid-upgrade projects across 26 states. $1.9B in federal funding within a $5.25B total (with recipient cost-share) is intended to reconductor/upgrade transmission lines and add over 23GW of capacity; formal award agreements expected Oct 2026–Jan 2027.

London-based AI "neocloud" building vertically integrated AI data centers, power infrastructure and large-scale GPU clusters (reportedly $103B+ in total contract value). Ahead of a planned NYSE listing (ticker NSCL), it raised $3.36B in pre-IPO convertible financing led by Third Point, including a $1B tranche committed by NVIDIA (due ~mid-November 2026).

New York-headquartered (Tel Aviv R&D) AI-native data security company founded 2021 by Yotam Segev and Tamar Bar-Ilan; offers data discovery, classification, DSPM and access-governance for humans, machines and AI agents. Raised a $400M extension from Goldman Sachs Alternatives on its Series G, pushing its valuation above $12B.

Utah-based industrial vehicle-automation company, maker of the Mobius fleet-orchestration platform for mining, defense and industrial equipment. SoftBank Group invested $225M and formed a joint venture with ASI to develop and commercialize autonomous heavy construction equipment (haul trucks, dozers, loaders) at scale.

AI data-labeling "data factory" startup supplying training data, tasks and rubrics for frontier and agentic AI labs. Raised $350M at a $3.5B valuation co-led by Insight Partners and S32; existing investor GV (Google Ventures, Alphabet's venture arm) participated alongside Greylock, Lightspeed and others. Note: the press release does not name Alphabet/Google directly, only its venture arm GV.

Cambridge, MA robotics/AI research institute founded in 2022 by Boston Dynamics founder Marc Raibert, spun out of Hyundai Motor Group with $400M+ in backing; works on robot control, perception, manipulation and "athletic intelligence." SoftBank has agreed to acquire RAI from Hyundai; financial terms undisclosed, deal under CFIUS review as of late September 2026.

Pharmacy-benefit-management and AI-driven care-navigation company helping employers manage pharmacy spend and member support. Raised $155M Series E led by Francisco Partners, with existing investors Thrive Capital and Khosla Ventures participating; the round values Rightway at $1.75B and brings total funding to about $281M.

Enterprise browser company ('Island Browser') repositioning as a control layer for employee and AI-agent activity inside organizations; customers include Pfizer, Chipotle, American Airlines and major banks. Raised $400M Series F led by Evolution Equity Partners, with Sequoia, Coatue, J.P. Morgan and others participating, at a $6.4B valuation (up from $4.8B in March 2025).

AI-security company protecting enterprise generative and agentic AI systems from poisoning, prompt injection and runtime attacks, including AI coding agents. Raised $100M Series B led by Delta-v Capital, with Ten Eleven Ventures, Morgan Stanley, M12 (Microsoft's venture fund) and Booz Allen Ventures participating, following a $6M seed and $50M Series A (total funding ~$156M).
